slides.main: Low FODMAP isn't the first step for IBS.
slides.sub: What guidelines say to try first, and when low FODMAP comes in.

slides.main: Eat regular meals and keep tea or coffee to 3 cups a day.
slides.sub: Also less alcohol, fizzy drinks and fatty food, and no more than 3 portions of fresh fruit a day.

slides.main: Gas and bloating: oats and up to 1 tablespoon of linseeds daily.
slides.sub: With diarrhea, avoid the sweetener sorbitol in sugar-free sweets, gum and drinks.

slides.main: Low FODMAP is a 2 to 6 week trial, ideally with a dietitian.
slides.sub: Then FODMAP groups come back one at a time. Not everyone with IBS improves on it.

slides.main: Don't go gluten-free before you have been tested for coeliac disease.
slides.sub: The test is only accurate while you eat gluten: in more than 1 meal daily for at least 6 weeks.

slides.main: Get medical advice if you have:
items: Blood in your stool or black stools
Symptoms that wake you up at night
Symptoms that first started after age 50
